<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <Description>
      This is the Azure.AI.VoiceLive client library for working with the Azure VoiceLive service.

      Azure VoiceLive is a managed service that enables low-latency, high-quality speech-to-speech interactions for voice agents. The API consolidates speech recognition, generative AI, and text-to-speech functionalities into a single, unified interface, providing an end-to-end solution for creating seamless voice-driven experiences.

      Use the client library to:

      * Create real-time voice assistants and conversational agents
      * Build speech-to-speech applications with minimal latency
      * Integrate advanced conversational features like noise suppression and echo cancellation
      * Leverage multiple AI models (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Phi) for different use cases
      * Implement function calling and tool integration for dynamic responses
      * Create avatar-enabled voice interactions with visual components

      See https://aka.ms/voicelivesdk-net for more information.
    </Description>
    <AssemblyTitle>Microsoft Azure.AI.VoiceLive client library</AssemblyTitle>
    <Version>1.3.0-beta.1</Version>
    <!--The ApiCompatVersion is managed automatically and should not generally be modified manually.-->
    <ApiCompatVersion>1.2.0</ApiCompatVersion>
    <PackageTags>Azure.AI.VoiceLive</PackageTags>
    <TargetFrameworks>$(RequiredTargetFrameworks)</TargetFrameworks>
    <IncludeOperationsSharedSource>true</IncludeOperationsSharedSource>
    <AotCompatOptOut>true</AotCompatOptOut>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <Compile Include="$(AzureCoreSharedSources)AzureKeyCredentialPolicy.cs" LinkBase="Shared/Core" />
    <Compile Include="$(AzureCoreSharedSources)AzureResourceProviderNamespaceAttribute.cs" LinkBase="Shared/Core" />
    <Compile Include="$(AzureCoreSharedSources)AzureEventSource.cs" LinkBase="Shared\Core" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <None Include="VoiceLiveClient.Overrides.cs" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Azure.Core" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>

limitations: Coverage is partial: 31 evidence items span 31 Customizations source paths among 474 eligible files and 547 discovered files. Excluded session commands/protocol/updates, WebSocket client overrides/helpers, VoiceProvider, options, logging and telemetry implementations prevent complete customization discovery; no package-wide absence claim is made.

All supplied source evidence is classified handwritten-marker under src/Customizations. The frozen .NET guideline provisionally treats non-Generated source as handwritten; no regeneration, generated-partial comparison or compiled API surface was inspected.

AzureRealtimeNativeVoice, AzureVoice and OpenAIVoice have empty bodies but explicit VoiceProvider base relationships, so proposals describe those declarations rather than assuming a demonstrated generator baseline change. The empty RespondingAgentOptions internal partial has no supplied active mapping/base change and is not counted as an independent behavior.

Constructor overloads with the same declared identity are grouped. Called generated collection constructors, content-part constructors, VoiceLiveClient delegated constructors and Argument.AssertNotNull implementations are excluded; documentation exceptions do not prove local null validation or complete constructor behavior.

Duration getters explicitly use zero for absent nullable backing values; setters explicitly cast TotalMilliseconds to float or int. No range checking, checked arithmetic, precision preservation, constructor-initialized default or service-side timing guarantee is established. InterimResponseConfigBase's two-second-default comment conflicts with its getter's local unset fallback and is not treated as measured behavior.

Union model storage/construction, named factory helpers, equality overrides and JSON codecs are distinct supplied surfaces. Their raw state combinations are not assumed valid or mutually exclusive beyond visible constructors. Numeric token values and tool names have no shown local range/name checks.

The codecs return null for unsupported JSON kinds, may propagate parsing/value-conversion failures, and in two cases can write no value for empty model state. RequireApprovalOption silently ignores unrecognized object properties and nonarray recognized properties; nonstring array entries may fail GetString. These are observed local branches, not claims that all invalid input succeeds.

The ToolChoiceFunctionObject implementation is excluded: only the custom codec's construction, WriteObjectValue delegation and read-time Name extraction are known. Wire fields, discriminator handling and the helper's validation cannot be inferred.

MaxResponseOutputTokensOption uses selected-state value comparisons but delegates GetHashCode to base; no consistent value-hash contract is claimed. The string inf/default-null factories describe local states, not measured server defaults or acceptance.

Point/list conversion is visible for both crop corners and checks two entries. Geometry, coordinate bounds, System.Drawing behavior and wire serializer activation are not independently observed. The two corner findings share ToPoint evidence without counting that helper as a third standalone customization.

Client source declares api-key and https://ai.azure.com/.default constants and credential fields, but supplied bodies do not show authentication execution or WebSocket transport setup. No additional Auth or streaming finding is inferred from these constants, a README example or missing partial implementations.

The source csproj reports 1.3.0-beta.1 and ApiCompatVersion 1.2.0 while latestRelease metadata reports 1.2.0. A TypeSpec location/emitter reference establishes generation context, not that supplied handwritten behavior matches every released version.

GeneratorAddressable yes means these constructor, inheritance, member-representation, union-codec and value/helper shapes could plausibly be generated. It is not evidence of current emitter support, a measured generator defect or a demonstrated removal opportunity.

Assessment covers only 31 frozen non-generated candidate fragments out of 474 eligible files; 23 named files were skipped for review budget and coverage is expressly partial. No package-wide absence or exhaustive customization count is inferred.

Generated counterparts, generator outputs and the client/session implementation partials are not in the supplied SDK evidence; source declarations and documentation cannot establish whether a particular generated member was replaced, how wire mappings activate, or how WebSocket authentication operates.

The README documents client construction and WebSocket usage, and the csproj includes an explicit compile-related None entry, but neither establishes the behavior of skipped source files or runtime activation of the supplied model members.

No distinct missed customization was supported by the supplied fragments without duplicating a proposal identity; omissions are inconclusive and uncounted. Accepted and revised decisions are AI-reviewed, not human-verified; human overrides remain authoritative.
